page: Vultr voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is an entry-level memory-optimized cloud compute instance provisioned with 1 dedicated vCPU on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The single physical core provides 1 hardware execution thread supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. System memory measures 8.0 GB, establishing an elevated 1:8 core-to-memory ratio. Local persistence is supplied via 50 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage, and networking includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance boundaries. The instance demonstrates solid single-threaded computational efficiency, attaining top-quartile results in both Geekbench single-core testing (score 1999.0) and stress-ng single-core testing (2896.39). Conversely, overall system throughput is strictly bounded by the single-core topology, leading to bottom-quartile scores on aggregate multi-core tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and software compilation via Clang. Memory bandwidth reaches 22.42 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 20.94 GB/sec for writes, reflecting baseline throughput appropriate for entry-tier nodes.

Qualitatively, this server type delivers cost efficiency by pairing dedicated CPU execution with a relatively large 8 GB memory capacity without requiring the procurement of additional unneeded CPU cores. Given this configuration and its storage profile, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive background workers, small in-memory caching tiers, lightweight relational databases, and staging environments with single-threaded execution patterns.
